video_title: Wemby Skips Media After WORST Playoff Performance!

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Wembanyama needs to be aggressive and assertive early in Game 6
quotes.excerpt: When he's ultra aggressive, everybody has to conform to that. OKC has to conform to that.

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: We need the monster Wemby, right? Like he's got to come out from the jump.

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: I would agree. And that was more impactful to me than the referees. You just saw it in Game 4. When he's ultra aggressive, everybody has to conform to that. OKC has to conform to that, his teammates have to conform to that. He's such a dominant presence. When he decides that he wants to be aggressive, everybody has to deal with him. Now, when he's in a position where somebody has to facilitate like this, and he has to get his buckets off of somebody else making the play for him, they're just not as strong as a team. I didn't like the fact that he didn't have as many attempts in this game. I didn't feel like he was aggressive. A lot of his scoring and a lot of his impact came from the free throw line. I didn't love that. It just seemed like this was one of those games where he just floated through and he didn't find his aggression. He was looking for his aggression, he was looking for that power punch in the three-point line. And I didn't love that. He went 0 for 5 from the three-point line. You got to put more pressure on these guys at your size, how you've been able to dominate. You just got to be more assertive, you got to be more part of the offense, if not the offense, for this team to be successful and win games. So I expect him to adjust again in a pivotal Game 6, but last night, I just didn't see that fire and that fight like you just mentioned, Beadle, that we've seen up until this point for them to be the team that we've grown accustomed to them being.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Wembanyama's early aggression sets the tone and opens up the offense
quotes.excerpt: When Wemby is doing that, is when the whole floor opens up for this offense.
quotes.quote: I just don't it's not like they don't know how important it is to get him off to a good start and to have that energy. Even last night, I saw Chet, the first play of the game, he got the offensive rebound, took one dribble sideways backwards and took the shot. And he made it. I loved the fact that he did that after the question with SGA the night before, just to show that urgency and to show that I'm going to be aggressive tonight. And he did it, the first two or three plays of the game, he did that, got second attempts off his rebounds and put it up. That's what we need to see Wemby do in San Antonio because it just sets the tone for the entire offense. It makes the defense just put in such a confusing situation when you have this 7'6" guy that's just attacking non-stop. It opens up everything. It forces the defense to have to double team him. Then I think that's when Fox can get in the lane and get out in transition. That's where Harper's going to be great. That's where Castle can get downhill. When Wemby is doing that, is when the whole floor opens up for this offense. And it's just too pivotal of a game last night for him not to do that and only take 15 shots. I'll never think 15 shots is enough for Victor Wembanyama. He's too good, he's too dominant. I'm totally okay with him taking 25 to 30 shots a game and willing his team to a win because you know he's going to give the effort and the impact on the defensive end. That just comes with his size and his God-given talent on that side of the floor. He has to be just as dominant offensive, especially in this series with a team like OKC. He's got to be dominant and he's got to do it early. And I fully expect him to do that in Game 6. It's just weird to me he didn't do it last night.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Wembanyama's decision to skip media sparks debate on player accountability
quotes.excerpt: You have that obligation as a professional, as an NBA player, to make yourself available through the good, the bad, the ugly.

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: After the game, Wemby didn't talk to the media, which is crazy because he also won the award for best guy with the media and all that stuff. We haven't heard any reasons why yet, Lou. There's no medical reason that's been given to us. I don't know if he's just thought anything he would say was going to get him fined. I don't love it, especially in a Western Conference final. So go ahead, rip him.

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: Frustration. No, it's just frustration. We don't have to rip him. I just think we have to hold all of these guys accountable. We can't draw a line for one guy and then make excuses for another guy. We like to hear him speak, we like to hear his perspective, especially in a deep playoff series that's going on right now instead of leaving us to try to guess what he's thinking or what he's going through. Just step up to the podium for a few minutes and bite the bullet and give us the information that we're looking for, good or bad. We've accepted the fact that he can say some of these. Do it in French. Even if you don't want to do it. If you want to piss some people off, do it in French. But we got to hear from you after these games, especially with where you are in your career. You're still a young player in this league, and we want to hear your perspective. This is the series that everybody wants to watch, so they want to hear what you think about the referees, they want to hear about what you feel about your play, they want to hear about the adjustments you're going to make. All of those things are key when you're building your reputation. He also deserves to be frustrated as well and tonight just ain't the night, fine me, do whatever you want to do. I'm locked in on the mission, but it's fair to say we would love to hear from you after these games. I'm always pro player. I've had a hundred games where I didn't want to talk to the media. I don't feel any different about this.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: I understand where the frustration is coming from, but I can't get his back here. I think there's an obligation. I think there's a responsibility as the best player on that team, the only person probably on that team that the media wants to talk to afterwards, and you have that obligation as a professional, as an NBA player, to make yourself available through the good, the bad, the ugly. Not just when it's good, not just when you're at home when you're beating the drum with your teammates when you win. You have to do that when you lose. So I see why I've been frustrated too and I've probably dipped out of media before, but it's not right, especially when you're a guy of his stature and you're Victor Wembanyama. Everyone's going to want to hear from you after a big loss, after a huge win, it doesn't matter. You have to give them that respect and that courtesy to do that. So I didn't like this at all. You got to be better, you got to be more mature, especially now in the conference finals. People want to hear you talk when you win, when you lose, it doesn't matter. You have to give them that at least.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Biyombo and Plumlee's late-game fouls raise questions about Wembanyama's influence
quotes.excerpt: This did look a little weird to me. At the end of the game, he puts him in and he literally gives two cheap fouls.

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: Listen, I'm cool with it. All is fair in war. When we're going at it and we're trying to accomplish something, I'm cool with it. But don't do these type of things and then want to create a frenzy about not getting the calls and not shooting free throws and it's a physicality problem. I'm cool with all of this stuff, but just make sure you're cool with it too. That's my thing.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: He's the same guy that elbowed Naz Reid in the face. Same guy that jumped into SGA's leg. He's competitive, he's playing as hard as he can. Dirty, aggressive, whatever you want to call it. This did look a little weird to me. At the end of the game, he puts him in and he literally gives two cheap fouls. If this was somebody else, named, I don't know, Draymond Green, Dillon Brooks, someone with that reputation, not that he's anywhere near to those guys' reputation, but he's kind of dancing, he's kind of flirting with it with his antics in this postseason.

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: Could have any conversation about optics? Come on, man.
